title: Glintt's own healthtech products fill the slot its healthcare and pharmacy verticals would otherwise open
content:
Glintt's verticals — healthcare, pharmacy and retail — are among the most attractive in the pilot, and its tool field records the reason the row is still do-not-pitch: its platforms are its own healthtech products.

That combination is the recurring trap in this part of the dataset. Sector fit tells you the firm reaches the right buyers with the right process problems; business model tells you whether it can carry someone else's component to them. A product house monetises its own roadmap, so a component it adopted would compete for room against features it planned to build and sell itself.

PinkRoccade sits in exactly the same position on the Dutch side of the corpus, with ideal healthcare and municipal verticals and a product rather than custom-build model. Two independent rows arriving at the same conclusion suggests the constraint is structural in health and public-sector software: the firms closest to those buyers tend to own the software, not integrate it. The row otherwise remains a mechanically rescored v2 entry with an OSS-portfolio screen outstanding.
